subject: Accounting
title: Why Auditing Exists
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why Auditing Exists.

hook.text: A company says it earned $5 billion. How do you know it's telling the truth? You audit.

buildup.text: Auditing is the independent examination of financial statements to verify their accuracy.

discovery.text: It exists because of a trust gap—investors can't personally check every transaction a company makes.

twist.text: Without audits, financial markets would collapse. Nobody would trust any company's reported numbers.

climax.text: Auditors are the gatekeepers between companies and the investors who rely on honest reporting.

punchline.text: Trust but verify. That's the auditor's entire job.

quiz.question: Why does auditing exist?
options: To independently verify that financial statements are accurate

details.summary: Auditing exists because stakeholders — investors, lenders, regulators — need independent assurance that a company's financial statements are accurate and free from material misstatement, reducing information asymmetry between management and outsiders.
details.whyItMatters: Without auditing, investors would have to blindly trust management's financial claims, making capital markets unreliable and increasing the cost of borrowing and investment for every company.
takeaways: Auditing provides independent verification that financial statements are materially accurate
It exists to reduce information asymmetry between company insiders and outside stakeholders
Reliable auditing is essential for capital markets to function and for investors to make informed decisions

faq.question: Why can't companies just report their own financial results without auditing?
faq.answer: Companies prepare their own statements, but management has incentives to present results favorably. Independent auditors verify those statements to give investors and creditors confidence the numbers are reliable. Without this check, trust in financial reporting would collapse.

faq.question: Who benefits from auditing?
faq.answer: Investors get reliable information for decisions. Lenders assess credit risk accurately. The company benefits through lower borrowing costs that come with credible reporting. Employees and regulators also rely on audited statements for decision-making and oversight.
